label: original-phase input j/v/1/n/a/y/k/c (t>=3) in sequences starting with u/b/p/g/d/w
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase (99.8% of activation mass), never at t=0-1, rarely at t=2, and most often at orig_idx 4-7. Its rate rises with L. The current input token is the main driver: j (6.2x lift), v, 1, then n, a, y, k, c; it is near zero for m and x. Activation is much stronger when the sequence starts with u (5.6x), b, p, g, d or w, and when such tokens appeared earlier in the sequence. It is mostly active on the first occurrence of the input token. It is essentially silent on the delimiter and copy phases. It acts like a graded conjunction of current input identity and earlier-context identity, so a boolean predicate captures only part of it: on dev, the input set alone gives recall 0.88 at precision 0.12, and adding the first-token condition gives P 0.40 / R 0.58 / mass recall 0.68. The top activations (about 0.95-1.0 of max) are j/v/1/n/a inputs at t=5-7 in sequences starting with u or b.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: j, v, 1, n, a, y; least: s, 0, 2, u) and the first original token (most: u, b, p, g, w, d; least: 1, c, j, v); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, t=5, L=8 & t=7.
